answer_1.quote: In GLOBAL-GROUP, the LLM is given a pool of words, and with them, must create equal groups of words and provide a topic (oftentimes more abstract than just pertaining to semantic relatedness) that connects each group's words.
answer_1.outputs: The model outputs several groups of words, along with an associated topic for each group.

answer_2.quote: We use group-level F1 to compare each matched pair of predicted and true groups... We also evaluate the predicted group topics using a "Topic Achieved" (TA) score, a boolean indicating if a topic was successfully predicted.

answer_3.quote: During this process, if any game caused issues with answer parsing due to bad response formatting, the model response was reformatted via prompting of GPT-4o-mini.

answer_4.quote: two human annotators annotated the topic achievement of 200 Chinese grouping attempts... we calculated Randolph's Kappa between the annotators, treating automatic predictions... as one of the annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators were provided the same rules for calculating the Topic Achieved score but were asked to base it on their own perception of similarity.
